why_this_file_exists: ID-05's second clause forbids a cast that hides a genuine type error, and a
green typecheck is not evidence about that: `tsc` has no flag for `no as
never`. This baseline is what turns the count into a RATCHET: `pnpm typecheck`
fails if the number of non-test `as never` casts GROWS.
WHY A BASELINE AND NOT ZERO. The V1 case FAILed on this clause with 475
occurrences. Sweeping them is per-site review, not a mechanical edit: measured
on this tree, two instances of the SAME syntactic shape behave differently --
removing both casts from `ctx.plugin(storageJsonPlugin as never, { root } as
never)` compiles clean, while removing only the config cast from
`ctx.plugin(Storage, {} as never)` reports TS2345. A gate that demanded zero
today would be a gate nobody could pass honestly. A gate that forbids GROWTH is
enforceable now and is the property that stops the hole widening.
measured_by: helpers/typecheck.mjs (escapeHatchGate), comments stripped, non-test src only

justified.revealed_error: TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'SessionId' (and, once the id is branded, TS2740: the literal is missing 24 members of the `Session` class)
why_left_in_place: This cast hides a REAL error, so it is not justified as clean. It is left in
place because the honest fix is not type-level: `createRun` takes a real
`Agent` whose `session` is the `Session` CLASS with 24 required members, and
this crash rig fabricates a header instead of creating an Agent. The sibling
(`concurrency.test.ts:151`), which requires mounting the AgentLoop into a rig
whose child is SIGKILLed mid-run -- a topology change to a crash test, outside
ID-05's type-level scope. Recorded as a finding rather than silently widened.
justified.reachability: NOT REACHABLE from the product: `durability-runner.ts` is absent from the package's `exports` and has no production importer (`durability-advanced.test.ts:1080` asserts this). It is a hand-run CLI. So this is an oracle violation in a test rig, not a product defect -- both facts are true and the distinction is the finding.

why_left_in_place: Removing it compiles clean, so it is redundant rather than masking. It is not
removed here because the probe's INTENT is to read a tool name that is
deliberately outside the typed tool catalog (`v4_target` is registered at
runtime by the probe), and `ctx.tools.get` is keyed on the known tool-name
union. The cast documents that the name is intentionally outside the catalog.
Either form compiles; this one keeps the intent visible. It is counted in the
baseline so the ratchet accounts for it rather than silently tolerating it.
justified.reachability: NOT REACHABLE from the product: a hand-run probe file, no production importer.

how_to_add_a_justified_cast: 1. Add an entry here with file, line, the verdict, the error that removing it
reveals (or `none`), and why it is not a mask.
2. Raise `non_test_as_never_count` by one IN THE SAME COMMIT, so the
justification and the permission are reviewed together.
3. `pnpm typecheck` then passes. A cast added WITHOUT this edit fails the gate.
NEVER `as any`, and never an inline `@ts-ignore`: the point of the ratchet is
that the cast stays VISIBLE and REVIEWED.
